name: SessionStore
purpose: Issue, rotate, and revoke server-side session records keyed by high-entropy identifiers, with fixation resistance and explicit lifetime boundaries.
api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Session:
    id: str
    subject: str
    created_at: int
    idle_expires_at: int
    absolute_expires_at: int

class SessionStore(Protocol):
    def create(self, subject: str) -> Session: ...
    def load(self, session_id: str) -> Session | None: ...
    def rotate(self, session_id: str) -> Session: ...
    def revoke(self, session_id: str) -> None: ...
    def revoke_all_for_subject(self, subject: str) -> int: ...
invariants: Session ids MUST carry ≥128 bits of entropy from a CSPRNG and MUST NEVER encode user-controlled input.
On privilege elevation (login, role change, MFA step-up) the session id MUST be rotated; the prior id CANNOT be reused.
Sessions MUST expire at min(idle_timeout, absolute_timeout); server-side revocation MUST win over client-held cookies.
Session cookies MUST be set Secure, HttpOnly, and with SameSite=Lax or Strict; Domain SHALL NEVER be broader than the application host.
revoke_all_for_subject() MUST terminate every live session for that subject atomically and MUST be invoked on password change.
load() MUST NEVER extend a session past absolute_expires_at even on activity.
extension_contract: Storage backends register as session-store adapters (redis, postgres, signed-cookie) implementing the Protocol. Adapters that cannot perform server-side revocation (pure signed cookies) are forbidden from binding when revoke_all_for_subject is required by policy.

sources.locator: V3 Session Management Requirements (V3.2 Session Binding, V3.3 Session Logout)

why_essential: Fixation, idle timeout, and subject-wide revocation are the shared burden of every authenticated product; without a shared store each team reinvents one missing control and the security posture decays to the weakest.
alternatives_considered: Pure JWT sessions with no server state — cannot revoke without a parallel denylist.
Framework default session middleware — often lacks idle-plus-absolute dual clock.
Sticky-session in memory — fails revoke_all_for_subject under horizontal scale.
